forTheReviewerAndTheArchitect: packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile:767 keeps LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/sjawhar/legion as a literal, so after the transfer a build from cybermonklabs/legion would push ghcr.io/cybermonklabs/legion-worker carrying a source label naming the old repository, and GitHub would not link the package to its repository. The implementer recorded this as an open question for the architect and gave the reason as 'no build passes --build-arg'; that reason is inaccurate - worker-image.yaml:235-237 already passes a labels: block to docker/build-push-action, with org.opencontainers.image.revision and org.opencontainers.image.version in it, and a buildx --label overrides a Dockerfile LABEL of the same key, so the fix is one line in a step the build job already runs and needs no build argument. I did not record it as a test failure: the spec's Change bullet enumerates the image paths, the plugin download address, the npm repository field and the docs site, and this pull request's own AGENTS.md rule says 'never written as a literal in a workflow or in the docs config' - a Dockerfile is neither, and nothing in this repository reads that label (docs/kubernetes.md's acceptance reads org.opencontainers.image.revision). It is a scope decision, which is the architect's.

A configured pair whose two names are both repositories the project really serves is accepted and silently merges them wherever a name is compared: logUnservedRenames warns only when the `to` is NOT served, so the opposite case gets no warning. That is operator error rather than a defect - the pair means 'one repository' by definition, --check-config prints every pair, and the whole feature is configured by an operator - but it is the one misconfiguration the file accepts quietly.

appauth's alias is per owner, not per repository, and that is why it is safe: a pair is an alias only when the `from` owner owns no repository the project serves (`all[from]` is false). Before the transfer, when the project still serves sjawhar/legion, `!all[to]` already skips the pair, so a pair configured early changes nothing for gh or git - confirmed above by the two bundles. Where both owners are served the conflict is logged once and each owner keeps its own token, which is documented in credential.go.
